items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I’m very lucky to have the help of Jami Dauber who’s been acting as our band manager and road manager for quite a while. She’s played trumpet in the band like 23 years.

ctx.x: Well man, that’s a great question. What I do spend a lot of my time as the sole booker of the DIVA jazz orchestra and my quintet, Five Play. And I’m a co-leader with a new trio called the 3-D Jazz Trio. So I spend ages and endless amounts of hours and weeks and months and years trying to book those groups. Aggressively. I mean that was part of my day job you know, as a band leader without a booking agency. So in the end sometimes I’d be easily eight hours a day, especially booking a tour, even working on a two…

things out. And I’m like man, and I’m getting these little goose bumps sometimes when I’m very enthusiastic about something. And that for me was like oh my God this is so great. Like I actually love the drums again. I love the drums so much. Because when you’re the band leader sometimes there’s just so much other stuff going on I, anyway, forget like I love playing the drums and this is what I’ve done since I was eleven years old. So not being distracted by, “Oh no, we don’t have another gig.” “Oh no, we’re going…
Well that’s one upside. I’m curious what does a drumset player practice for five hours?
